subject: SLA amendment request — uptime threshold & monthly remedy cap
messages:
From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahq.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Marcus Green <m.green@novahq.com>, NovaHQ Legal <legal@novahq.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA ask: uptime floor and monthly credit cap

Hi Irene,

Thanks for the demo last week — team was impressed with the latency profile. Procurement and legal reviewed the standard SLA and asked if Redwood would consider a few amendments before we move to signature:

- Uptime floor: 99.95% (we'd like this reflected in the Master Services Agreement)
- Monthly remedy cap: fixed at 10% of monthly fees (we're trying to limit credit exposure)
- Maintenance carveout: scheduled maintenance up to 6 hours/month with advance notice
- Latency: we want a p95 guarantee for the public API endpoints used by our customer-facing features (we can share the endpoint list)

I'm attaching NovaHQ_SLA_Redlines_20260926.pdf with our redlines. Can you review and let us know what is feasible? If you prefer, happy to do a 30-minute call with procurement/legal tomorrow morning.

Looking for a quick turnaround — our go-live target is mid-October.

Best,
Sofia Ramirez
Sr. Procurement Manager | NovaHQ
sofia.ramirez@novahq.com
Attachment: NovaHQ_SLA_Redlines_20260926.pdf

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahq.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor and monthly credit cap

Hi Sofia — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks.

I'll run this with our product & legal leads (looping Laura and Karthik) and come back with a consolidated response. High-level notes up front: we can discuss uptime thresholds and credit caps, but both impact pricing and operational commitments.

Quick question: when you say p95 guarantee for public API endpoints, do you mean p95 latency on hosted API (shared tenancy) or specific dedicated routes? That changes possible carveouts and pricing.

If you're available, let's tentatively book 30 minutes Monday 9:30am PT to align.

Cheers,
Irene
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 27 Sep 2026 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: NovaHQ SLA request — suggested counterproposal

Team — quick internal thread summarizing NovaHQ's asks (see redlines attached). My suggested counterproposal below; please review and flag legal/pricing concerns.

Proposed Redwood counter (for discussion with NovaHQ):
- Uptime floor: 99.92% (we can protect our operational surface without committing across bursty batched inference patterns)
- Monthly remedy cap: 15% of monthly fees (we can cap exposure while keeping economic upside for pilot customers)
- Scheduled maintenance carveout: up to 12 hours/month with minimum 48-hour notice (we accept less friction for planned ops)
- Latency SLOs: offer p95 < 220ms for hosted API under typical traffic; offer an optional dedicated-latency pilot for p95 < 120ms at a committed monthly spend (details to be priced separately)
- Exception: latency guarantees exclude large-scale model upgrades and regional network incidents beyond Redwood's control; we will provide runbooks and outage reports for material incidents.

I built a short counterproposal PDF (Redwood_SLA_Counterproposal_20260927.pdf) with fallback language and a variant for dedicated capacity pricing. Key asks for NovaHQ: a 6-month pilot commitment for dedicated latency routes (if they want the tighter p95).

Two quick questions for legal/pricing:
1) Is a 15% monthly cap within our acceptable risk envelope?
2) Any reason we can't agree to 12 hours maintenance carveout rather than 6?

If this looks reasonable I'll send to Sofia and Marcus and propose a 45-day pilot/PO box for the latency-critical endpoints.

— Irene
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Counterproposal_20260927.pdf

From: Marcus Green <m.green@novahq.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahq.com>, NovaHQ Legal <legal@novahq.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor and monthly credit cap

Irene — thanks for the quick response and the proposed counter. A few points from our side: 

- NovaHQ cannot accept below 99.95% uptime for our production contract; our customers require this level of availability and it's in our own SLAs.
- 15% cap is closer, but we prefer 10% as a hard cap — our finance team can't absorb larger uncertainty in credits during the pilot ramp.
- Regarding maintenance: we could flex to 10 hours/month if necessary, but prefer 6.
- For latency: the hosted p95 < 220ms is fine as a baseline, but the tighter p95 < 120ms must be deliverable on production endpoints without a multi-month pilot; we need a 30-day canary at minimum.

If Redwood can accept 99.95% + 10% cap + maintenance <= 10 hours/month, we can push to procurement approval this week. Otherwise we'll need to revisit commercial terms.

Can we do a call tomorrow 9am PT with legal to triage redline language?

Thanks,
Marcus Green
Head of Platform Partnerships | NovaHQ
Attachment: None

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Green <m.green@novahq.com>, Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahq.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, NovaHQ Legal <legal@novahq.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Sep 2026 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA ask: uptime floor and monthly credit cap — compromise proposal

Marcus / Sofia — thanks for the clear constraints. We discussed internally and want to close quickly to meet your October go-live. Proposed compromise below (if acceptable we'll ask legal to convert to tracked redlines):

- Uptime floor: 99.92% measured monthly (Redwood operationally can guarantee this with described exclusions).
- Monthly remedy cap: 15% of monthly fees; remedy accrues monthly and is capped at 15% (we can include a clause to roll forward unused remedy to the next month once during the first 3 months of the contract).
- Scheduled maintenance: up to 10 hours/month with 48-hour notice; critical security patches may be outside this window but will be communicated.
- Latency: p95 baseline for hosted API < 220ms; for p95 < 120ms we will offer a 45-day dedicated-latency pilot priced at a fixed monthly rate (pilot terms will be attached as an addendum). If Redwood cannot meet the dedicated pilot SLO at the end of 45 days, NovaHQ will receive a one-time remediation credit equal to 10% of the pilot month fee.

Action items:
1) If NovaHQ agrees in principle, please confirm and we'll have Legal produce tracked redlines including the remedy cap language and maintenance carveouts.
2) We'll provision a HubSpot deal milestone and a DocuSign envelope for the addendum.
3) If you want the dedicated-latency pilot, we'll need endpoint whitelist and traffic profile by EOW (Friday).

I'm optimistic this is a reasonable middle ground — it reduces Redwood's exposure while giving NovaHQ clearer predictability. Happy to jump on the call tomorrow 9am PT to finalize language.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
